articles.title: Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg placed on leave
articles.summary: Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg claims the company’s chief financial officer “conspired” with board members to place him on leave, 404 Media reports.
articles.body: Matt Mullenweg, the CEO of WordPress.com owner Automattic, has been placed on a paid leave of absence, as reported earlier by 404 Media. In an internal message by the outlet, Mullenweg claims Automattic chief financial officer Mark Davies “conspired” with board members to place him on leave. “They voted to put me on a paid leave of absence. I voted against that,” Mullenweg wrote, referring to Davies, along with Automattic board members Ann Dunwoody, Toni Schneider, and Sue Decker, 404 Media reports. Mullenweg, who also co-founded WordPress.org, has headed up Automattic since 2014. In 2024, Mullenweg waged a public pressure campaign against a prominent WordPress host, a move that divided the open-source community and ignited a legal battle that’s still going on today. Automattic spokesperson Megan Fox confirmed the company’s decision in an emailed statement to The Verge. “Matt Mullenweg is currently on leave from Automattic,” Fox writes. “Mark Davies, Automattic’s CFO, will lead the company as interim CEO. The Board has full confidence in Mark’s leadership and in the team’s ability to execute against the company’s priorities.” Mullenweg will remain on Automattic’s board, 404 Media reports. “Automattic’s board has decided to ask Matt to step away from his CEO role and take a leave of absence,” Schneider said on the company’s internal message board, according to 404 Media. “We have asked Mark Davies to assume the interim CEO role while Matt is out. We’ve worked closely with Mark over the years and we’re confident he will steer the ship well while Matt is away.” Update, September 9th: Added Automattic’s statement.

articles.title: Apple unveils foldable phone as Ternus takes stage: 5 takeaways
articles.summary: Apple rolled out its next generation of the iPhone, AirPod and Apple Watch, with the company’s first-ever foldable smartphone taking center stage on Wednesday. The “Surprise and Shine” event marked John Ternus’s first public appearance as Apple’s new chief executive, offering a glimpse into how the product designer is approaching the next chapter for the…
articles.body:
Apple rolled out its next generation of the iPhone, AirPod and Apple Watch, with the company’s first-ever foldable smartphone taking center stage on Wednesday.

The “Surprise and Shine” event marked John Ternus’s first public appearance as Apple’s new chief executive , offering a glimpse into how the product designer is approaching the next chapter for the company.

The biggest launch of the day was the long-awaited iPhone Duo, marking the technology giant’s first foldable smartphone .

The Duo with 256-gigabyte storage will start at $1,999 — the most expensive sticker price to date for an Apple iPhone. The price for a 2-terabyte iPhone Duo will jump to $3,199.

The Duo, which will be available on Oct. 23, is a book-style foldable, similar to the size of a passport when opened. It has a bendable display and has the largest iPhone screen ever, Apple said.

The Duo is Apple’s biggest hardware change since the Vision Pro was released in 2023.

Ternus said the new phone “will redesign the experience of using a foldable phone.”

“Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together,” Ternus said. “This results in a square screen that’s rarely suited for the way people use them.”

When open, a user can multitask on multiple screens, while dragging content from one to the other much like computer windows. According to Apple, the display is 50 percent larger than the new iPhone 18 Pro Max and 80 percent larger than the iPhone 18 Pro, both of which were unveiled earlier in the presentation.

“We brought together thoughtful design with breakthrough engineering in a way only Apple can, and the result is a series of remarkable innovations that we believe will redefine the experience of using a foldable phone,” Ternus said.

While the iPhone Duo marks the highest sticker price for an iPhone, Apple also raised base-level prices for the new iPhone 18 lineup and older generations.

The new iPhone Pro starts at $1,199 and the Pro Max model starts at $1,299, while the iPhone 17, iPhone Air and iPhone 17e, which were released last year, were raised by $100 each.

This is a change for Apple, which usually lowers the prices of older generations once a new lineup is released.

Analysts predicted Apple would announce new price hikes this week as the AI boom fuels massive demand for memory chips, which store and process data in most electronics. The ultra-fast pace of AI development has strained supply and driven up costs.

Earlier this year, then-CEO Tim Cook warned price hikes were “unavoidable” due to the demand. The company raised MacBook and iPad products by $150 to $300 in June.

The launch event had a new host this year, with Ternus making his first public appearance as CEO of Apple on Wednesday. It comes just week one after longtime CEO Tim Cook handed over the reins to Ternus, a product designer who has worked at Apple for the last 25 years.

Cook made a cameo in the introduction video, which featured various characters debating the way to start a movie. At one point, Cook says, “Camera follows a mysterious figure before revealing our main character. … No, no, no, not me. That’s your guy. That’s your opener.”

The camera then panned to Ternus, who said, “I want to take a moment to express what an extraordinary privilege it is to represent the remarkable teams here at Apple.”

While Cook previously served as Apple’s chief operating officer, tackling sales, operations and supply chain logistics, Ternus’s 25 years at Apple were spent on hardware and product design. The new CEO played a major role in the expansion of Apple’s hardware, working on products like the iPad and AirPods.

Most recently serving as the company’s senior vice president of hardware engineering, Ternus is largely expected to lead with product design in mind and is under pressure to tackle the company’s lagging development of artificial intelligence.

Ternus stands behind Apple’s AI strategy

Amid scrutiny over Apple’s approach to AI, Ternus doubled down on the company’s strategy, while emphasizing the company’s hard-line stance on privacy.

In his first few minutes Wednesday, Ternus said AI “makes entirely new kinds of experiences possible, and AI can become even more useful when it brings together your life with the apps, services and products you use every day.”

The new CEO said he thinks of a product as an “intelligent hub” that is “deeply personal” and integrated across multiple devices, apps and services.

“In other words, you would arrive at something remarkably familiar, because there’s no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iPhone,” Ternus said.

“As your personal hub, your iPhone can do so much more for you because it understands your context. This includes your calendar, your relationships, your routines, the most private details of your daily life,” he added.

It remains to be seen how updates to Apple Intelligence, the company’s personal intelligence system, will push the company forward as competitors at the frontier labs develop at a much faster pace.

As concerns mount over how AI firms collect users’ data to personalize experience, Ternus touted that Apple Intelligence runs on-device “whenever it can.”

“When greater capability is needed, private cloud compute extends that same level of privacy protection, ensuring that nobody — not even Apple — can access what’s yours. It’s personal intelligence that’s actually personal,” he said.

Apple scales up health features in wearables

Apple also announced a series of new health features available on its newest Apple Watch and AirPod models.

Health technology wearables have become widely popular in recent years, offering a range of analytics for users to keep better track of their heart health, sleep and exercise.

The new Apple Watch Series 12 features a new “Health Sensing System” that Apple claims has the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable. The company also improved the watches’ heart rate variability measurements with new sensors and LED lights, providing 60 times more frequent heart rate readings than the Series 11.

The company also introduced a new readiness feature that estimates a user’s “capacity to take on the day.” This numeral score takes into account a user’s recent activity, vitals and sleep, and adjusts throughout the day.

Using Apple’s new Siri AI, the Series 12’s built-in microphone will “help you make sense of what you hear in a private and secure way.” Siri Recap will be able to summarize chats, revisit old conversations, while sound recognition can help those who are deaf or hard of hearing listen for sounds like sirens, crying babies and doorbells.

As for the AirPods 5, Apple is introducing live translation, the ability to listen on multiple AirPods and isolate your voice to reduce background noise.

images.caption: Apple CEO John Ternus speaks during an announcement of new products on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, in Cupertino, Calif. (AP Photo/Jeff Chiu)

articles.title: NASA wants to see your pictures of the sky. Here’s why
articles.summary: NASA wants you to point your phone to the sky and take a picture of the clouds. For science.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – NASA wants you to point your phone to the sky and take a picture of the clouds. For science.

Starting on Sept. 15, the space agency’s PACE satellite (which stands for the Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem satellite) will circle the Earth every 98 minutes. While it’s overhead, the satellite will be collecting important environmental data, measuring how clouds and particles in the atmosphere absorb and reflect sunlight.

Here’s where you (and everyone else on land) comes in: Scientists want to compare what they’re seeing in the sky with what you’re seeing on the ground.

The pictures will help researchers to better understand the far-away images they’re capturing from space, said Dr. Andrew Sayer, the PACE atmosphere lead. Because each pixel in the PACE satellite images represent a distance of about 0.75 miles across, ground observations will give more detail and help fill in the gaps.

“We want to be able to identify whether or not each pixel in a satellite image is a cloud or not, because if it’s cloudy we want to determine the properties of that cloud, and if it’s not cloudy we want to determine the properties of the atmosphere and surface underneath the cloud. … So the ground observers will help us to assess that.”

Download the Globe Observer app and set an alert for when the PACE satellite is passing overhead. “Timing is critical!” the researchers say, so make sure you’re ready.

Five minutes before PACE passes overhead your location, head outside and get in position for your cloud observation.

When you’re ready for your observation window, click the “Clouds” tool.

Collect the cloud photos in the six directions as instructed by the app.

The researchers ask you only take and submit cloud photos during daylight hours, not at night. More details about how to participate can be found online here .

The project runs through Oct. 15, so you have a month to participate once the project kicks off.

The PACE satellite launched in 2024 with the goal of observing our atmosphere and oceans in close detail from 420 miles away.

“It’s going to be an unprecedented view of our home planet,” said project scientist Jeremy Werdell when the satellite launched.

Scientists hope these observation help improve weather forecasting, including the timing of hurricanes and toxic algae blooms.

images.caption: In this image taken from NASA video, the Pace (Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, Ocean Ecosystem) satellite detaches from a SpaceX rocket in orbit, Thursday, Feb. 8, 2024. NASA’s newest climate satellite rocketed into orbit Thursday to survey the world’s oceans and atmosphere in never-before-seen detail. (NASA via AP)

articles.title: US announces $45m in security funding, additional naval vessels for Ecuador
articles.summary: Secretary of State Rubio has hailed Ecuador as the US’s ‘most involved and aggressive partner’ in the anti-drug fight.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump’s administration will seek $45m in security funding for Ecuador, as part of its cooperation with the country’s right-wing government.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the pledge during a visit to the Ecuadorian capital, Quito, on Wednesday.

He also praised the government of Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa as being “the most involved and aggressive partner” the US has had in its work dismantling criminal networks and “bringing people to justice that have never been brought to justice before”.

In addition to the $45m security package, Rubio said the Trump administration would launch a $10m initiative to tackle illegal gold mining, gang recruitment and drug trafficking.

It would also give a coast guard cutter ship and five interceptor vessels to help Ecuador’s navy, adding to previous seven previous vessels the US delivered earlier this year.

Rubio’s stop in Ecuador is part of a larger three-day, three-country visit to South America , which already took him to Colombia. On Thursday, he will continue to Peru.

Security has been a dominant theme so far on his trip. The US has sought to increase its influence across the Western Hemisphere, taking increasingly aggressive military actions abroad in the name of combatting crime.

The Trump administration has also labelled multiple Latin American criminal organisations “foreign terrorist organisations”.

“These are not ordinary groups. Clearly, they engage in common crime, but they have terrorist capabilities across the region, and that must be confronted,” Rubio said in Quito. “They must be dismantled, they must be defeated, and we are committed to doing that.”

As part of Wednesday’s stop, Rubio designated Los Tiguerones, an Ecuador-based drug trafficking ring, as a “foreign terrorist organisation”, accusing the group of trafficking illegal narcotics and being involved in the violent takeover of a television station in 2024.

Since 2023, Ecuador has taken an increasingly hardline shift under Noboa.

The youngest president in his country’s modern history, Noboa was first elected to complete after the government was abruptly dissolved in 2023. To secure his re-election in 2025, Noboa leaned into security concerns, pledging a stern crackdown.

Ecuador has seen a spike in crime since the COVID-19 pandemic, with drug-trafficking organisations making increasing use of its Pacific ports.

To address that issue, Noboa has deployed thousands of military service members and police to crime-ravaged areas. He has also called the conflict with drug-traffickers a “state of war”.

That approach aligns closely with the Trump administration’s security platform, and the two countries have forged close relations since Trump’s return to office in 2025.

In March, for instance, the US confirmed it was engaged in joint military operations with Ecuador.

Right-wing governments in the region, including Noboa’s, have also joined the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition (ACCC), a regional security framework created and led by the Trump administration.

More recently, Ecuador has been collaborating with the US on efforts to intercept and attack boats allegedly tied to narcotics trafficking.

On Tuesday, for instance, the US intercepted a vessel it said had links to the criminal group Los Choneros, transferring the suspects to Ecuadorian authorities. It was the sixth such operation in less than two weeks.

Both the US and Ecuador have been accused of human rights violations as part of their anti-narcotics operations.

The US, for instance, has carried out roughly 68 lethal boat strikes in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific Ocean since September 2, 2025, in a campaign aimed at eliminating “narco-terrorists”.

More than 220 people have been killed in those operations. Some families, including in Ecuador, have accused the Trump administration of attacking and killing fishermen who had no connections to drug trafficking.

An Ecuadorian survivor of a US boat strike was transferred back to his country in October 2025, where he was later released from custody due to a lack of evidence. Legal experts have likened the attacks to extrajudicial killings, in violation of international law.

Rubio, however, used his visit to defend the boat-bombing campaign. “Our goal is not to go after fishermen. Our goal is to go after drug traffickers,” he said.

images.caption: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is welcomed by Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa at Carondelet Palace, the seat of Ecuador's government in the capital, Quito, on September 9 [AFP]

articles.title: Trump Urges Voters to Let Him ‘Finish the Job’ at GOP Convention
articles.summary: President Donald Trump asked supporters at his midterm convention to consider November’s elections a referendum on his presidency, while acknowledging it may...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump asked supporters at his midterm convention to consider November's elections a referendum on his presidency, while acknowledging it may take voters time to feel the benefits of his policies.

The unusual high-profile gathering in Dallas of lawmakers, cabinet officials, and donors comes as Trump and his party face substantial headwinds ahead of Election Day. With polls showing Trump's popularity at record lows and Americans of different political persuasions troubled by his handling of the war in Iran and economy, he needs a jolt of energy to help his allies maintain control of Congress.

If Trump was hoping to dispel a sense of foreboding, his trip to Texas on Wednesday got off to a rocky start.

Before boarding Air Force One to depart the Washington area, an emergency inflatable slide deployed, delaying the president's departure. Trump said it was for an inspection; a person familiar with the matter said military personnel accidentally triggered the slide.

The president also conceded to reporters that efforts to push down gas prices might not bear fruit until after the midterms, a theme he returned to in his speech as he asked voters to keep faith in — and help bolster — his agenda.

"I want you to remember me in four or five years when this country is rocking — remember, I'm the one that got it started," Trump said.

In his prime time speech, Trump highlighted his accomplishments: securing an overhaul of the tax code, brokering prescription drug price cut deals, and increasing energy production. It amounted to an attempt to rally his base to turn out in November, albeit with a message that may not be as well received by voters worried about the cost of living and the war.

He also planned to propose making his tax cuts permanent and cutting credit card swipe fees in a bid to address affordability concerns, according to excerpts released by the White House.

"Your vote will decide whether our country stumbles at the starting gate of our next 250 years or surges forward and never ever looks back," Trump said from the stage at the American Airlines Center.

The president has promised to travel extensively in the run-up to the election to help Republican candidates in tight races across the country, and on Wednesday said he expected to make some 35 trips to support the GOP in key races. But he also signaled some of his campaigning might be virtual, and past promises to hit the trail have not always materialized.

images.caption: Trump Urges Voters to Let Him ‘Finish the Job’ at GOP Convention · Bloomberg · Photographer: Al Drago/Bloomberg
